review_type: Independent algebra and read-only protocol/code/result inspection; no new simulation or rerun of the numerical checker
conclusion: Formula and horizon cancellation verified under the listed assumptions; no blocking issue identified

definitions.h: single-cell probability of a living descendant at selection horizon T
definitions.A: probability all independent sister subtrees generated through t are extinct at T

assumptions: One founder at common known calendar time zero
Nonnegative locally bounded deterministic calendar-time rates shared by all living cells
Independent binary daughters; no interactions or informative observation losses
Future-blind uniform sister tag; after tag death the family may still survive
Any-descendant family survival selection; equally weighted founders
Positive family inclusion probability; compare identical absolute t with T>=t

algebra_checks.identity: Substitution cancels z(0) and yields displayed Q independent of T for t<=T
lambda identically zero or mu identically zero gives Q=1 through T
Unequal rates give hypoexponential survival; equal positive rates give exp(-k*t)*(1+k*t)
For t>T the actual tagged survival is Q_T(T)*exp(-(M(t)-M(T))), rather than continuation of the two-state formula

rate_exchange_counterexample.type: Exact analytic corollary, not part of the frozen numerical grid
rate_exchange_counterexample.conclusion: Arbitrary schedule exchange is not symmetric; the endpoint survivor function is not determined by L(T),M(T) alone.

reviewed_numerical_check.implementation_review: Correct backward ODE, Poisson-functional integral, direct cumulative-rate expression and independent forward-chain equation; piecewise ODE and quadrature boundaries handled explicitly.

scope_limits: Not cell-age hazards or inherited states
Not founder frailty or averaged random environments
Not a mixture of unmatched founder-entry calendar times
Not interactions, informative censoring or absent branches
No claimed biological mechanism, priority or clinical applicability
Endpoint Q_T(T) need not be invariant as T itself changes
empirical_implication: Horizon invariance cannot alone establish constant biological rates. Rejecting this model requires an explicit prediction test with an identified observation process.
